arxiv-2108-03281.title: Globally optimizing QAOA circuit depth for constrained optimization problems
arxiv-2108-03281.creator: Rebekah Herrman, Lorna Treffert, James Ostrowski, Phillip C. Lotshaw, Travis S. Humble, George Siopsis
arxiv-2108-03281.description: Abstract We develop a global variable substitution method that reduces n n -variable monomials in combinatorial optimization problems to equivalent instances with monomials in fewer variables. We apply this technique to 3 3 -SAT and analyze the optimal quantum circuit depth needed to solve the reduced problem using the quantum approximate optimization algorithm.

arxiv-2209-05142.title: The role of entanglement for enhancing the efficiency of quantum kernels towards classification
arxiv-2209-05142.creator: Diksha Sharma 1, Parvinder Singh 2, Atul Kumar 1
arxiv-2209-05142.description: Abstract Quantum kernels are considered as potential resources to illustrate benefits of quantum computing in machine learning. Considering the impact of hyperparameters on the performance of a classical machine learning model, it is imperative to identify promising hyperparameters using quantum kernel methods in order to achieve quantum advantages.

arxiv-2305-01521.title: Unlocking the Power of Representations in Long-term Novelty-based Exploration
arxiv-2305-01521.creator: Alaa Saade, Steven Kapturowski, Daniele Calandriello, Charles Blundell, Pablo Sprechmann, Leopoldo Sarra, Oliver Groth, Michal Valko, Bilal Piot
arxiv-2305-01521.description: Abstract We introduce Robust Exploration via Clustering-based Online Density Estimation ( RECODE ), a non-parametric method for novelty-based exploration that estimates visitation counts for clusters of states based on their similarity in a chosen embedding space. By adapting classical clustering to the nonstationary setting of Deep RL, RECODE can efficiently track state visitation counts over thousands of episodes.

arxiv-2405-12391.title: Automated Anomaly Detection on European XFEL Klystrons
arxiv-2405-12391.creator: A. Sulc, Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin für Materialien und Energie, Berlin, Germany A. Eichler, T. Wilksen, Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron, Hamburg, Germany
arxiv-2405-12391.description: Abstract High-power multi-beam klystrons represent a key component to amplify RF to generate the accelerating field of the superconducting radio frequency (SRF) cavities at European XFEL. Exchanging these high-power components takes time and effort, thus it is necessary to minimize maintenance and downtime and at the same time maximize the device’s operation.

arxiv-2408-14617.title: Dynamic Locality Sensitive Orderings in Doubling Metrics
arxiv-2408-14617.creator: An La, Hung Le
arxiv-2408-14617.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by An La, Hung Le. In their pioneering work, Chan, Har-Peled, and Jones (SICOMP 2020) introduced locality-sensitive ordering (LSO), and constructed an LSO with a constant number of orderings for point sets in the d d -dimensional Euclidean space. Furthermore, their LSO could be made dynamic effortlessly under point insertions and deletions, taking O ⁡ ( log ⁡ ( n ) ) O(\log(n)) time per update by exploiting Euclidean geometry.

arxiv-2511-21548.title: Metastability of diffusion processes in narrow tubes
arxiv-2511-21548.creator: Wen-Tai Hsu
arxiv-2511-21548.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Wen-Tai Hsu. We study the metastable behavior of diffusion processes in narrow tube domains, where the metastability is induced by entropic barriers. We identify a sequence of characteristic time scales { T ϵ i } 1 ≤ i ≤ | V ′ | \{T_{\epsilon}^{i}\}_{1\leq i\leq\absolutevalue{V'}} and characterize the asymptotic behavior of the diffusion process both at intermediate time scales and at the first critical time scale.

arxiv-2606-30075.title: Programmable generation of flying cat-qubits
arxiv-2606-30075.creator: Cecilia Erneman, Zeidan Zeidan, Göran Johansson, Maryam Khanahmadi

pmc-10527678.title: An Approach for the Estimation of Concentrations of Soluble Compounds in E. coli Bioprocesses
pmc-10527678.creator: Deividas Masaitis, Renaldas Urniezius, Rimvydas Simutis, Vygandas Vaitkus, Mindaugas Matukaitis, Benas Kemesis, Vytautas Galvanauskas, Benas Sinkevicius
pmc-10527678.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Accurate estimations of the concentrations of soluble compounds are crucial for optimizing bioprocesses involving Escherichia coli (E. This study proposes a hybrid model structure that leverages off-gas analysis data and physiological parameters, including the average biomass age and specific growth rate, to estimate soluble compounds such as acetate and glutamate in fed-batch cultivations We used a hybrid recurrent neural network to establish the relationships between these parameters. To enhance the precision of the estimates, the model incorporates ensemble averaging and information gain.

pmc-10647549.title: Assessing Vehicle Wandering Effects on the Accuracy of Weigh-in-Motion Measurement Based on In-Pavement Fiber Bragg Sensors through a Hybrid Sensor-Camera System
pmc-10647549.creator: Xinyi Yang, Xingyu Wang, Joseph Podolsky, Ying Huang, Pan Lu
pmc-10647549.description: Weigh-in-motion (WIM) systems are essential for efficient transportation and monitoring parameters such as vehicle number, speed, and weight to ensure regulatory compliance and enhance road safety. Recently, WIM measurements using the Glass Fiber Reinforced Polymer Fiber Bragg Grating (GFRP-FBG) sensors have shown robustness and effectiveness.

pmc-11314644.title: Dune Morphology Classification and Dataset Construction Method Based on Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Orthoimagery
pmc-11314644.creator: Ming Li, Zekun Yang, Jiehua Yan, Haoran Li, Wangzhong Ye
pmc-11314644.description: Dunes are the primary geomorphological type in deserts, and the distribution of dune morphologies is of significant importance for studying regional characteristics, formation mechanisms, and evolutionary processes. Traditional dune morphology classification methods rely on visual interpretation by humans, which is not only time-consuming and inefficient but also subjective in classification judgment.

pmc-11451138.title: Effect of an educational intervention based on health belief model on preventive behaviors against malaria in over 18-year-old Afghan immigrants living in Parsian
pmc-11451138.creator: Zhila Pasalari, Roghayeh ezati rad, Zahra Hosseini, Habibolah Torki, Amin Ghanbarnejad, Teamur Aghamolaei
pmc-11451138.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundMalaria disease is one of the most dangerous protozoan parasitic infections with a high mortality rate in developing countries. Malaria is a public health issue, especially in Hormozgan province, and is highly affected by foreign immigrants (Pakistani and Afghani); thus, the present study aimed to evaluate the effect of an intervention based on the health belief model (HBM) on the promotion of malaria prevention behaviors in Afghani immigrants over the age of 18.

pmc-12462485.title: Fragmentation and multithreading of experience in the default-mode network
pmc-12462485.creator: Fahd Yazin, Gargi Majumdar, Neil Bramley, Paul Hoffman
pmc-12462485.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Reliance on internal predictive models of the world is central to many theories of human cognition. Yet it is unknown whether humans acquire multiple separate internal models, each evolved for a specific domain, or maintain a globally unified representation. Using fMRI during naturalistic experiences (movie watching and narrative listening), we show that three topographically distinct midline prefrontal cortical regions perform distinct predictive operations.

pmc-12481064.title: Current therapeutic strategies in Parkinson’s disease: Future perspectives
pmc-12481064.creator: Tae Young Kim, Byoung Dae Lee
pmc-12481064.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the loss of dopaminergic neurons and the accumulation of misfolded α-synuclein. Current treatments, including dopaminergic medications and deep brain stimulation, provide symptomatic relief but do not halt disease progression. Recent advances in molecular research have enabled the development of disease-modifying strategies targeting key pathogenic mechanisms, such as α-synuclein aggregation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and genetic mutations, including LRRK2 and GBA1.

pmc-12539266.title: Single-nucleus profiling of Ossabaw pig atherosclerosis model
pmc-12539266.creator: Olga Bondareva, Marlene Hausner, Manuela Konert, Daniela Branzan, Katharina Noreikat, Susann Oßmann, Levani Sopromadze, Antonia Geisler, Peter MH Heegaard, Bilal N Sheikh, Sabine Steiner
pmc-12539266.description: SummaryAtherosclerosis is a major cause of cardiovascular disease, and accurate preclinical models are essential for developing effective therapies. The Ossabaw pig model has high potential due to its physiological similarity to humans, but its molecular characterization remains limited. To address this, we performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing of over 36,000 nuclei from aortas of Ossabaw pigs fed chow or atherogenic diets.

pmc-12592517.title: The association of the rumen virome with methane emissions in dairy cattle
pmc-12592517.creator: Carlos Navarro Marcos, Mónica Gutiérrez-Rivas, Idoia Goiri, Aser García-Rodríguez, Óscar González-Recio
pmc-12592517.description: Enteric methane production in ruminants is a major environmental concern, yet its association with the ruminal virome remains largely unexplored. Here, we conduct a bioinformatic analysis on previously published ruminal metagenomes from 448 Holstein cows to investigate the virome and its association with methane production. We identify 8933 viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs), including bacteriophages, archaeophages, megaviruses, and virophages.

pmc-12682694.title: To Migrate or not to Migrate? Exploring the Genomic Basis of Partial Migratory Behavior in Bats
pmc-12682694.creator: Diego M Peralta, Juan P Jaramillo-Correa, Helena S Hernández-Rosales, Juan I Túnez, Jaime Gasca-Pineda, Rodrigo A Medellín, Luis E Eguiarte
pmc-12682694.description: Migration is a widespread phenomenon in animals that involves the synchronized movement of numerous individuals across habitats. While migratory traits appear to be environmentally triggered, evidence also points to a still poorly understood genetically regulated mechanism. The study of both the genomic architecture of migration and the degree of similarity across migrating taxa is a recurrent topic in evolutionary biology.

pmc-12684300.title: Deciphering Ball Milling Mechanochemistry via Molecular Simulations of Collision‐Driven and Liquid‐Assisted Reactivity
pmc-12684300.creator: Rupam Gayen, Leonarda Vugrin, Zehua Zhang, György Hantal, Ivan Halasz, Ana‐Sunčana Smith
pmc-12684300.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Mechanochemistry by ball milling proceeds through a series of discrete, high‐energy collisions between milling balls and the sample, yet the molecular‐level processes that govern the resulting chemical and physical transformations remain poorly understood. In this study, we develop a molecular dynamics simulation protocol to investigate a model mechanochemical reaction between potassium chloride (KCl) and 18‐crown‐6 ether, both under dry conditions and in the presence of water as a liquid additive.

pmc-12821318.title: Short-form video overuse and adolescents’ restrained eating: the roles of body shame and physical exercise
pmc-12821318.creator: Xu Kong, Mingwei Deng, Sicheng Xiong, Chengwei Zeng, Zuhua Zhang, Chunling He, Bin Zhang
pmc-12821318.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe social media’s dissemination of norms for body shape is progressively shaping individual perceptions and behaviors. Social media plays a key role in causing body shame and restrained eating behavioral pattern of adolescents. Although the relationships among short-form video overuse, body shame, and restrained eating are well documented, it is unclear whether the specific problem of short-form video overuse also plays a role in these relationships.

pmc-13354310.title: Television (TV) Food Commercials Target Children: A Content Analysis of TV Food Advertisements in Iran
pmc-13354310.creator: Maryam Amini, Mehrnoosh Shafaatdoost, Delaram Ghodsi, Mohadese Borazjani, Maryam Aghayan, Nastaran Shariatzadeh
pmc-13354310.description: Background:This study aimed to analyze the content of Iran’s television (TV) food advertisements directed at children in 2020.Methods:All the programs broadcast on Channel II TV were downloaded for one week; however, only children’s programs were analyzed. The validated protocol was used to analyze the content of the advertisements.

pmc-13400848.title: Draft genome sequence of Pseudonocardia alni M29 isolated from healthy maize plant
pmc-13400848.creator: Deepak Singla, Shaloo Verma, Jagriti Yadav, Murugan Kumar, Hillol Chakdar, Alok Kumar Srivastava
pmc-13400848.description: The genus Pseudonocardia is known for siderophore production that helps plants in iron uptake. In this study, we report the draft genome of Pseudonocardia alni M29 isolated as an endophyte from healthy maize plants. De novo genome assembly resulted in 53 contigs (>500 bp) with overall genome size of 5.96 Mb.

pmc-13578765.title: Tunneling nanotubes regulate mitochondrial homeostasis between glioblastoma and astrocytes, and between tumor cells in vivo
pmc-13578765.creator: Ines Saenz-de-Santa-Maria, Anna Pepe, Jean-Yves Tinevez, Christel Brou, Yakov Vitrenko, Thomas Cokelaer, Elizabeth Cohen-Jonathan Moyal, Roberto Weigert, Chiara Zurzolo
pmc-13578765.description: Tumor progression is driven by cancer cells’ ability to establish a cellular network through tunneling nanotube-like connections (TNTs), which enable mitochondrial exchange both within the tumor cells and with the tumor microenvironment (TME). However, the functional consequences of mitochondrial transfer between tumor and non-tumor cells, and its occurrence in vivo, remain poorly understood.

uslaw-usc-t10-s935.title: 10 U.S.C. § 935 — Art. 135. Courts of inquiry
uslaw-usc-t10-s935.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s935.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part II (Personnel); Chapter 47 (Uniform Code Of Military Justice); Subchapter XI (Miscellaneous Provisions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Courts of inquiry to investigate any matter may be convened by any person authorized to convene a general court-martial or by any other person designated by the Secretary concerned for that purpose, whether or not.
